title: Your first day as a Muslim
whyMatters: The first day after Shahada can feel joyful, emotional, confusing, or all three within an hour. This step keeps that day simple. Protect your faith, keep the pressure off, and pick a few calm things to do next.

exactActions.text: Do not pile on obligations yet
subSteps: Remind yourself that Islam is learned over years, not in an afternoon.
Write down two things you believe clearly right now.
Stay out of online debates and long argument threads today.

exactActions.text: Pick one person you can lean on
subSteps: A local imam, a mentor who works with new Muslims, or a steady Muslim friend all work.
Ask them to help you with Ghusl and the first basics of prayer.
If you do not know anyone yet, phone a nearby masjid or email an organization that teaches beginners.
Nobody needs to hear this today except the people you choose.
If your safety at home is a concern, make a plan before you say anything.
Keep your first explanation short and about you.
Ask Allah for guidance, steadiness, and good people around you.
Use your own language if Arabic still feels foreign.
Say it again whenever the anxiety comes back.

timeEstimate: 20 to 40 minutes of planning, then rest

obstacles.problem: I feel pressure to become perfect right away
obstacles.solution: That pressure teaches you nothing. Start with faith, purification, the basics of prayer, and someone to ask. The rest arrives one piece at a time.

obstacles.problem: I do not know who to trust
obstacles.solution: Start with a local masjid, a named organization, or a qualified teacher. Steer clear of anonymous accounts that pressure you, shame you, or drag you into arguments.

tinyVersion: Today: say a simple dua, pick one person you can contact for help, and stop there.
unlocksNext: A calm first day makes Ghusl and the early prayer practice much easier to walk into.

commonQuestions.problem: Do I need a certificate today?
commonQuestions.solution: A certificate can help later for marriage, Hajj, Umrah, or some community records, but your Islam does not depend on paperwork. Ask a local masjid if you need documentation.

contextNotes.title: If you live with family
contextNotes.body: Do not risk your safety to make an announcement today. Speak to a mentor you trust first if you expect hostility.

contextNotes.title: If you are on your own
contextNotes.body: One email or one phone call to a local masjid is plenty for today. You do not need a whole network yet.

gentleScripts.title: To a mentor or masjid
gentleScripts.body: I recently became Muslim and I am looking for beginner help with Ghusl, prayer, and community support. Is there someone I can speak with?
